title: The Festering Fang
description: You picked up a strange "Dragontooth" while adventuring in Dragonspine. Perhaps you should ask around and see if someone knows anything more about it...

mainQuestExcel.title: The Festering Fang
mainQuestExcel.description: You picked up a strange "Dragontooth" while adventuring in Dragonspine. Perhaps you should ask around and see if someone knows anything more about it...

dialogs.text: Ah, I was hoping you'd swing by. Yes, about those Dragonteeth... Oh, I see you've already finished gathering them up.
When you were off exploring, I ended up hitting a slight snag over here... No matter what I hit this Dragontooth with, I simply cannot take so much as a sliver off of it.
I've never seen anything like this before, so I had someone talk to Mr. Albedo to see how we should deal with these materials.
And so, if you look over yonder, you'll see that Mr. Albedo had Miss Sucrose send over a Runestone. It's right on the Alchemist's Crafting Bench.
A Runestone? What's that got to do with our Dragonteeth?
Well, according to what Miss Sucrose relayed to us from Mr. Albedo, we need to give the material some special treatment before we can use it to forge weapons.
One of said methods is to have one Dragontooth absorb dragon-related "vitality," then used the vitalized Dragontooth to treat other Dragonteeth.

As for what Miss Sucrose said about the Runestone... Ah, yes, she said it was "a relic left to the Knights of Favonius by a wandering troupe that helped Mondstadt rebel against the old nobility a thousand years ago."
The flautist of that troupe once fought against a monster known as "Bakunawa" in the Mare Jivari. This Runestone was carved from its body...
Eh? Wait a sec, if Paimon's memory isn't failing her, didn't Citlali tell us that the Mare Jivari was created by Sanhaj's battle with the Abyss... five hundred years ago?
Are we sure the troupe's story is from a thousand years back?
Haha, how could it be mistaken? That wandering troupe's story of heroism has long since been recorded in the "History of Kings and Clans."
Anyway, Mr. Albedo said that this Runestone contains "infinite vitality," similar to that of a dragon.
All you need to do is use the Crafting Bench to absorb the vitality of the Runestone with the Dragontooth, then we can get to forging our weapons.
That sounds impressive... as expected of Albedo...
We'll have to thank him later.
#Yeah! If not for him, we'd be totally stuck... Anyway, {NICKNAME}, let's try absorbing the Runestone's power!
Haha, that's great! Here — you take this Dragontooth, and I'll leave that whole side of things to you.
Alchemy's truly something else, huh... How does one even absorb "vitality" from a thousand year-old stone?
Alrighty, I'll handle it.
You're back! How'd it go?
We didn't even get around to absorbing the "vitality"...
You tell Orban about what happened before...
I never expected something like that to happen... *sigh* I'm just glad you're safe and sound.
Oh no... You won't be able to use any Dragonteeth in your forging like this...
Don't worry. It's no skin off our backs.

flow.stepDescription: Obtain a Dragontooth that has absorbed power

dialogs.text: (The Runestone on the Crafting Bench emits a strange glow...)
Place the Dragontooth
Hey, Traveler, how'd it go? Did you let your Dragontooth absorb vitality from <color=#00E1FFFF>the Crafting Bench over there</color>?
This luster, this texture... Hoho, this is it!
Hahaha! I never knew alchemy could work such miracles. That's Mr. Albedo for you!
Thanks for your help. I can't work any alchemy to save my life. Right, now that we've got all the materials we need, give me a moment or two, and I'll get this weapon made right away...
Orban starts forging the weapon...
There, it's done! Haha! Here, hold that. How does it feel?
How much do I owe you?
Oh, don't worry about paying for it. The chance to work with these materials was a rare pleasure. No need to bring Mora into it.
Alright. I'd say this weapon is ready for an adventure, wouldn't you? I hope you'll take good care of it.
